analysis:
Only the test file provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift changed. The units supplied are BASE text for lines 3661-4499, the windowed-sidecar test suite (WS-4.2), plus a truncated patch excerpt. The changes appear to be test refactors, such as the productionWriteBehind helper and the head-side range 3685-3727. No production code is changed here. Because the excerpt is truncated and the head text for those ranges was not supplied, I could not inspect the new tests or any production changes directly.

The tests exercise security-relevant behavior under T-041 and TB-003: (1) tag domain separation between block and window HMAC tags (lines 3836-3848); (2) the sidecar AAD/plaintext header carrying only a keyed commitment (windowBaseTag) and never the absolute token position (3850-3893, 4341-4406), which is consistent with the T-041 requirement that nothing prompt-derived beyond the keyed lookupTag be added to the metadata; (3) fail-closed handling of a corrupted sidecar, which is unlinked and de-indexed (4041-4085); (4) the feature being off by default (4087-4110); (5) endurance-budget priority of blocks over sidecars (4239-4293); (6) TTL refresh of sidecars (4295-4337); and (7) a bounded stage cost for window reads (4427-4498).

These tests strengthen the T-041 mitigations. No security regression is introduced in the supplied evidence. The window sidecar is an at-rest artifact, and the threat model does not yet mention a sliding-window sidecar (windowKind 'sliding-window-v1'). Its plaintext discriminator is accepted by the test comments. The next pass should check whether the production sources that implement it (SSDBlockStore, SSDLookupKeys, SSDWindowSidecar) are in the PR, and whether T-041 should be updated to document them. The test at lines 4193-4235 pins the replay bound, so a restored window does not advertise a shorter bound.
